C.title: C. Reading
C.instruction: Read the passage and answer using evidence from the text. Each question is worth 4 marks.
C.passage: A regional service office publishes a guide saying that its new request form guarantees a reply within two days. The trial behind that statement involved ten requests: eight received a reply within two days and two took longer. A separate staff note records fewer clarification emails, while interviews with four applicants describe the form as easier to follow. The editor separates those outcomes rather than treating them as three proofs of the same claim. The office agrees to retract the guarantee. A proposed replacement says that replies may take longer, but the editor asks for the observed result as well, so that caution does not become vague. The revised guide states the trial figures and identifies the next action for applicants whose requests remain unanswered. A short public version and a longer explanatory note retain the same factual core. The longer note explains the trial’s limitations; neither version claims that the form alone caused faster replies. The editorial rationale records why the universal claim changed and why the distinction between ease of use and response time remained.

questions.question: What trial result contradicts the guarantee?
Which two other outcomes appear in the sources?
Why does may take longer alone not satisfy the editor?
What must the short and long versions share?
Which causal claim is avoided?

E.title: E. Writing
E.instruction: Write an editorial rationale for revising the service-office guide. Include an accurate replacement for the guarantee, distinguish the three source outcomes and explain how the short version can remain accessible without changing certainty or scope.
